question.text: Which of the following cartesian diagrams represent a function from X to X.

solution: X = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}. A function needs each element of X to appear exactly once as a first coordinate.
Diagram (1): the dots are (3,5), (4,4), (2,3), (1,2), (3,2). The element 3 appears twice, with images 5 and 2, and 5 has no dot. So it is not a function.
Diagram (2): the dots are (1,3), (2,3), (3,3), (4,3), (5,3). Each of 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 appears exactly once. So it is a function.
Diagram (3): the dots are (1,1), (2,2), (4,4), (5,5). The element 3 has no dot. So it is not a function.
Only diagram (2) represents a function from X to X.

checks.resolve_answer: Only diagram (2). Diagram (1) has two dots at x = 3, namely (3,5) and (3,2), and no dot at x = 5. Diagram (2) has exactly one dot for each x from 1 to 5, all at y = 3. Diagram (3) has no dot at x = 3.

question.text: Is every relation a function? Explain your answer and give examples.

answers.answer: No. A relation is a function only if every element of X appears exactly once as a first projection; for example {(1,2),(1,3)} is not a function, but {(3,3),(4,5),(5,4),(6,5)} is.
solution: A relation from X to Y is a function if each element of X appears only once as a first projection in the ordered pairs.
So a relation is not a function if an element of X has two different images, or if an element of X has no image.
Example of a relation that is not a function: with X = {1,2,3}, R = {(1,2),(1,3),(2,3)}. The element 1 appears twice as a first projection, so it has two images, 2 and 3.
In the same way, the cartesian diagram with dots at (3,5) and (3,2) is not a function, because 3 has two images.
Example of a function: f = {(3,3),(4,5),(5,4),(6,5)} on X = {3,4,5,6}. Each element of X appears once as a first projection. It does not matter that 4 and 6 both have image 5.
Answer: No, not every relation is a function. A relation is a function only when each element of X has exactly one image.

checks.resolve_answer: No. A relation is a function only if every element of X appears exactly once as a first component. Example of a function: $\{(1,2),(2,3),(3,3)\}$. Example of a relation that is not a function: $\{(1,2),(1,3),(2,4)\}$, since 1 has two images (2 and 3). Also a relation where some element of X has no image is not a function.
